more_info.overview: Agar is used as an emulsifier in food. Its technological role is to help oil and water remain mixed.
more_info.uses: EU permissions include unflavoured live fermented cream products and substitute products, both with a fat  content of less than 20 %, jam jellies and marmalades and similar products, other similar fruit or vegetable spreads. These permissions depend on the food category and its conditions of use.
more_info.origin: Extracted from suitable red seaweeds. The purified material is a galactose-rich polysaccharide.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specified starting material is plant derived and compatible with vegetarian and vegan diets. The specification does not establish halal or kosher certification.
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA found no concern for assessed food uses.
Human short-term studies and high-dose animal studies reported no relevant adverse effects.
